author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Makkot 16a he explains the views of R-Y and R-A [the supplied initials ר״י ור״א]: “For example, he accepted betrothal for her from another.” Rava objects: “If you appointed him an agent…” (Hyman says the Gemara mistakenly reads Rav and that Seder HaDorot needlessly struggles with this.) Rav Shimi of Nehardea then explains the case differently. Hyman states that Rav Shimi of Nehardea lived in Rava’s time.
In Pesachim 42b he explains the “scribes’ paste” as the depilatory preparation used by wealthy men’s daughters. Rav Oshaya the later explains it instead as cobblers’ paste.

notes.text: The checked Makkot discussion concerns Yohanan and Resh Lakish; the supplied second initial is ר״א, not ר״ל, so it remains a source question. The printed קלון is read in its Pesachim context as kolan, paste, not disgrace.

No new primary scalar was returned. מחוזנאה is kept as Mahozna’a in the heading rather than losing the initial mem in Chozna’a; the conventional Mahoza association is not fresh geographic proof. Supplied ר״י ור״א remains beside the earlier reported Yochanan/Resh Lakish discussion. Hyman owns the Rav-to-Rava correction, polemic against Seder HaDorot and dating of Shimi of Nehardea. אי שויתיה is quoted as If you appointed him, not a newly gendered She. The paste/depilatory/cobbler interpretations are inherited context, not a new Pesachim inspection; full Rav titles and later-Oshaya qualifier remain.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 1116) also has ר״י ור״א. Makkot 16a discusses Rabbi Yochanan and Resh Lakish earlier, and Rabbi Elazar asks Rabbi Yochanan a question in the exchange leading into Rav Shimi’s answer. The initials are retained. The consulted text reads Rav for the objection and explains the agency as the woman appointing the man to accept betrothal on her behalf. It then gives Rav Shimi of Nehardea’s separate answer. Pesachim 42b reads קולן and contrasts Rav Shimi’s depilatory interpretation with Rav Oshaya’s explanation of the paste used by cobblers and also by scribes to join paper.
